# Bicycle Fleet Maintenance

The shared bicycle fleet is inspected every second Tuesday by a rotating pair of volunteers
from the facilities team. Tyre pressure, brake pad wear and chain lubrication are checked
against a printed list pinned inside the maintenance shed door, and any bicycle failing more
than one item is tagged and pulled from circulation until a mechanic can look at it properly.
Spare inner tubes and a hand pump are kept in a labelled box on the second shelf, available to
anyone who needs a quick roadside repair rather than waiting for the scheduled inspection day.
Riders are asked to report a flat, a slipping gear or a loose seat as soon as it happens rather
than leaving a note for the next inspection, since a fault left unreported tends to get worse
over the following weeks and turns a five-minute fix into a full afternoon in the shed.
